Chosen from a fresh census (scripts/vr-blank-pair-census.mjs): every federal measure-and-issue pair in the live record whose row prints nothing, ranked by distinct members with a row. The pairs above 109 members are all ones earlier slices skipped, and their reasons still hold. At 109 members there are twenty new pairs on seven House bills. Twelve take a line here, on five acts; eight are skipped. None stores a `did`, so each line is written from its own mapping rationale (quoted here, with the file that stores it). `term` is the stored words the line carries and `termIn` names the field. Tense follows the stored outcome: all five acts passed the House only and open "Would". The FY2026 NDAA (H.R. 3838) is skipped because its stored status (enacted) conflicts with the archive's record that the law is S. 1071. None of the five acts carried a line before, so no line names a tally. `acts` carries every mapping on each act that takes a line. `skipped` lists every census pair at 109 members or more left blank, and why. No score, weight, mapping or key is read from or written to here.

H.R. 1048|119.title: Defending Education Transparency and Ending Rogue Regimes Engaging in Nefarious Transactions (DETERRENT) Act
H.R. 1048|119.summary: Strengthens Section 117 of the Higher Education Act by lowering the threshold for universities to report foreign gifts and contracts from $250,000 to $50,000 — and to $0 for "countries of concern" (China, Iran, North Korea, Russia). Requires disclosure of individual gifts to faculty and staff in a searchable database, adds endowment-investment transparency for large private institutions, and enforces compliance with fines and potential loss of Title IV funding. Passed the House 241–169; awaits Senate action.

issues.rationale: Core purpose: force disclosure of foreign money flowing to universities, faculty, and endowments.
Sets federal higher-education policy, backed by fines and Title IV enforcement for noncompliant institutions.

H.R. 1526|119.title: No Rogue Rulings Act of 2025
H.R. 1526|119.summary: Limits federal district courts to issuing injunctive relief that applies only to the parties before the court, curtailing nationwide ("universal") injunctions. Creates an exception routing multi-state challenges to executive actions to a randomly assigned three-judge panel. Passed the House on a near party-line vote; awaits Senate action.

issues.rationale: Bars a district court from granting injunctive relief broader than the parties before it, ending the nationwide injunction — the principal judicial remedy for halting federal action while it is challenged. Recorded as a yea cutting against judicial checks on the executive; supporters make the opposite case, that one district judge should not set national policy. Re-keyed from checks_balances in the August 2026 taxonomy split so that only members who took a position on court orders are judged by it. Weight 100 and primary status preserved.
A structural change to how courts issue relief; supporters call it a reform of judicial overreach.

H.R. 1919|119.title: Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act
H.R. 1919|119.summary: Prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC), maintaining accounts directly for individuals, or offering retail financial products, without explicit authorization from Congress. Framed by supporters as protecting financial privacy from government surveillance; critics say it forecloses a tool other central banks are exploring. Passed the House on a near party-line vote; awaits the Senate.

H.R. 1949|119.title: Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act of 2025
H.R. 1949|119.summary: Removes the Department of Energy's separate approval requirement for natural-gas imports and exports and gives the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) sole authority to approve the siting, construction, and operation of LNG terminals — while directing that exports be deemed consistent with the public interest. Supporters call it a way to speed U.S. energy exports and cut red tape; critics warn it sidelines review of price and emissions effects. Passed the House; awaits the Senate.

H.R. 471|119.title: Fix Our Forests Act
H.R. 471|119.summary: Overhauls management of federal forests to reduce catastrophic wildfire risk: designates high-risk "fireshed management areas," creates an interagency Fireshed Center to map and predict fire, expedites environmental review of forest-thinning and hazardous-fuels projects, and tightens court timelines for challenges to those projects. Passed the House with bipartisan support; awaits Senate action.
